talks.title: Keynote
talks.teaser: Discusses keynote and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Personal Journey Into Security

Ken Weston keynotes BSides Portland with an Alice in Wonderland “rabbit hole” theme. A Portland native with dysgraphia, he found computers gave him a voice, leading from web development and a sake brewery online store through startups to security work.

What Rabbit Holes Mean

In security, rabbit holes describe hyperfocus—sometimes productive, sometimes leading to burnout. Weston ties the metaphor to experimentation, community support, and a field where people innovate by using technology in unintended ways.

Investigations and Innovation

He recounts building USB-based tracking tools for stolen devices, presenting at DEF CON 23, media attention, a failed startup, and later work at Tripwire. Investigations rarely start from one alert; analysts pivot across data sources, building “crazy walls” of linked evidence like detectives.

Forensic Mindset

Weston introduces Edmond Locard as foundational to criminal forensics, framing investigation as creative synthesis across disparate clues rather than purely technical checkbox work.

talks.title: Delete Your Data
talks.teaser: Reviews delete Your Data and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Delete Your Data Mission

Recent law graduate Jacob introduces Delete Your Data, a Las Vegas nonprofit helping individuals request removal of personal information from companies and websites nationwide.

Simple Workflow, Legal Backbone

Users submit requests via the site; a scraping service locates accounts or the user specifies targets, then the organization sends deletion demands grounded in privacy law—not a purely technical delete button.

Statutory Rights

GDPR grants EU residents a right to be forgotten, and many vendors extend similar language globally. California's CCPA applies to large for-profit collectors meeting revenue or data-sale thresholds; Virginia and Colorado add state regimes, with Colorado notably covering nonprofits.

Privacy Policy Enforcement

Companies' privacy policies and terms form enforceable promises; the FTC Act bars deceptive practices when policies are ignored. Regulators and new laws also push readable policies—Flesch scores show Facebook, Reddit, and YouTube policies far above recommended seventh-grade readability.

talks.title: Live, Laugh, Lyrical Injection: Hacking Karaoke for Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Outlines live, Laugh, Lyrical Injection: Hacking Karaoke for Fun and Profit and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Karaoke as protocol

Security engineer Nate Norton humorously maps karaoke to infosec: sessions, hosts, guests, DNS, and APTs (advanced persistent talkers). He claims two unpatched vulnerabilities—weak authentication and lyrical injection.

Weak authentication

Anyone can write any name on a signup slip and receive a microphone—no validation—escalating to stage privileges. He demonstrated at DEF CON hacker karaoke using his real name for attribution, then pivoted to an unofficial talk.

Lyrical injection kill chain

Lyrical injection replaces a popular song's lyrics/melody with another track's words on timing, causing denial-of-service confusion that can spread to the audience. Norton walks through recon, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, C2, and objectives using the Lockheed Martin cyber kill chain. Mitigations are weak—projected lyrics, mic ducking, or acceptance.

talks.title: Smokeloader: The Pandora’s box of tricks, payloads and anti-analysis
talks.teaser: Outlines smokeloader: The Pandoras box of tricks, payloads and anti-analysis and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Meet SmokeLoader

Proofpoint reverse engineer Pim Jarabek dissects SmokeLoader, a long-running crimeware loader sold on underground forums with modular plugins. Though his day job focuses on botnets like Amadey and IcedID, SmokeLoader's anti-analysis tricks make it a standout case study.

## Modular Malware Business

Forum listings advertise plugins including form grabbers (HTTP POST credential theft), network password sniffers, and other commodity features. Buyers must crypt/pack samples themselves—the authors explicitly warn the raw build is not FUD.

## Packing and Staging

Jarabek explains the onion-like layers: a packed on-disk sample unpacks to an initial stager, which runs environment checks before loading the final in-memory payload. Understanding each stage is essential for analysts who never see the unobfuscated binary on disk.

## Anti-Analysis Focus

The talk emphasizes tricks that stall sandboxes and researchers—delays, integrity checks, and plugin architecture that complicates automated detonation. For defenders, SmokeLoader illustrates why loader analysis must go beyond surface-level AV signatures.
